title: Multimode squeezed light generation and characterization
authors: Alexander Chudakov, Vladislav Severin, Anastasia Poshevkina, Danil Malyshev, Kirill Kuznetsov, Olga Tikhonova, Dmitry Kalashnikov, Polina Sharapova
abstract: Nowadays, the realization of quantum computations and communications based on continuous variables has attracted a significant attention due to a substantial expansion of the system dimensionality. The main progress in this area is attributed to the implementation of multimode systems based on squeezed states of light. One of the simplest ways to generate such states relies upon their producing in a single-pass optical parametric amplifier (OPA) using ultrafast pumping. However, for homodyne detection of such multimode states, the profile of the local oscillator (LO) must perfectly match the profile of the measured mode. Usually, this is not the case; therefore a proper treatment of multimode squeezing is required. In this work, we study both theoretically and experimentally the multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II OPA. We characterize such sources and investigate the degree of squeezing in dependence on the LO spectral profile, employing a pulse shaping technique. The theoretical analysis is performed using the Schmidt-mode theory. This work might have a significant impact on the realization of multimode quantum protocols
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical and experimental study of multimode squeezed light generated using Type-0 and Type-II Optical Parametric Amplifiers. By employing Schmidt-mode theory and pulse shaping, the authors characterize the squeezing in relation to the local oscillator's spectral profile. The results confirm the feasibility of generating and measuring these complex quantum states, which has implications for advanced quantum protocols.
main_problem: The paper theoretically and experimentally characterizes multimode squeezed light generated via Type-0 and Type-II Optical Parametric Amplifiers (OPAs). It specifically investigates how the measured squeezing depends on the spectral profile of the local oscillator (LO).
main_result: The study successfully characterizes the multimode squeezing for both PDC types, showing good agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements, while also analyzing the impact of optical losses.
method: The analysis employs Schmidt-mode theory for theoretical modeling and uses homodyne detection combined with pulse shaping techniques for experimental characterization.
model_or_system: The system involves generating multimode squeezed light using Type-0 and Type-II PDC in a single-pass OPA. The theoretical framework utilizes the Schmidt-mode decomposition of the Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA) to diagonalize the effective Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Measured quadrature variance ($\Delta P_{LO}$), multimode squeezing parameter ($r_{	ext{dB}}$), and anti-squeezing ($	ext{ASq}$) values.
important_parameters: LO spectral profile, coupling strengths ($\Gamma$), detection efficiency (e.g., 70%), and the type of PDC (Type-0 vs. Type-II).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific commutation relations for the Schmidt operators and incorporates losses into the variance calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optical setup, Joint Spectral Intensities (JSIs) for both PDC types, Schmidt modes, and the measured/calculated squeezing and anti-squeezing across multiple Hermite-Gaussian (HG) modes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from theoretical modeling using Schmidt-mode theory to detailed calculations for Type-0 and Type-II PDC, followed by an experimental section detailing the setup, measurements, and comparison of results with theory.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, providing detailed methods for characterizing complex, multi-mode quantum states generated in nonlinear optical processes.
